glosses: fright, alarm (sudden surprise with fear or terror)

examples.text: У неё на лице́ изобрази́лся испу́г.
Испу́г смени́лся ра́достью.
Вдруг в окне́ разда́лся стук, тако́й гро́мкий и необыча́йный, что Саве́лий побледне́л и присе́л от испу́га.
examples.translation: Suddenly there was a knock at the window, so loud and unusual that Savély turned pale and almost dropped backwards with fright.
examples.english: Suddenly there was a knock at the window, so loud and unusual that Savély turned pale and almost dropped backwards with fright.

glosses: внезапное чувство страха
A state of terror excited by the sudden appearance of danger; sudden and violent fear, usually of short duration; a sudden alarm.

examples.text: With a bolt of fright he remembered that there was no bathroom in the Hobhouse Room. He leapt along the corridor in a panic, stopping by the long-case clock at the end where he flattened himself against the wall.

glosses: Someone strange, ugly or shocking, producing a feeling of alarm or aversion.

examples.text:
Her maids were old, and if she took a new one,
You might be sure she was a perfect fright;
She did this during even her husband's life
I recommend as much to every wife.

glosses: To frighten.

examples.text: Are not you he […] That frights the maidens of the villagery […] ?
Little Miss Muffet, She sat on a tuffet, Eating of curds and whey; There came a little spider, Who sat down beside her, And frighted Miss Muffet away.

A very fine situation was proposed to him, where he might have a noble view of the ocean; but he started back, with an attitude of terror Betterton might envy, when Hamlet meets his father's ghost, and cried out,—"Oh, Christ! the sea looks so fierce that it frights me!

glosses: frightened; afraid; affright

examples.text: Don't be fright, it is not so impossible as it seems.
Don't be fright, I'm not going to hurt you.

He had a great heavy jaw and shoulders like an ox and bore no resemblance to Maurice Leonard. 'Come along, lad,' the sergeant said. 'Come along. Don't be fright. It's what you're here for now, ain't it?'

glosses: A summons to arms, as on the approach of an enemy.

examples.text: Arming to answer in a night alarm.

glosses: Any sound or information intended to give notice of approaching danger; a warning sound to arouse attention; a warning of danger.

examples.text: Sound an alarm in my holy mountain.
She went about the house in a state of real terror, and yet lied monstrously and wilfully, and invented many of the alarms she spread, and made many of the sounds we heard.

glosses: A device intended to warn or give notice of approaching danger.

examples.text: The fire alarm is located high on the wall to prevent tampering.

glosses: A sudden attack; a disturbance.

examples.text:
Lord Marshal, command our officers-at-arms
Be ready to direct these home alarms.

Is it then true, as distant rumours run,
that crowds of rivals for thy mother's charms
thy Palace fill with insults and alarms?

glosses: Sudden surprise with fear or terror excited by apprehension of danger; in the military use, commonly, sudden apprehension of being attacked by surprise.

examples.text: Alarm and resentment spread through the camp.

glosses: A mechanical device for awaking people, or rousing their attention.

examples.text: The clock radio is a friendlier version of the cold alarm by the bedside.

glosses: An instance of an alarm ringing, beeping or clanging, to give a noise signal at a certain time.

examples.text: You should set the alarm on your watch to go off at seven o'clock.

glosses: To call to arms for defense.
To give (someone) notice of approaching danger or necessary action; to rouse to vigilance; to put on the alert.

examples.text: The sudden drop in temperature should alarm you into taking precautions.
Her illness started to alarm the doctors, who ordered more tests.

When the carriage drew up in the grass-grown court yard before the hall-door, two lazy-looking men, whose appearance well accorded with that of the place which they tenanted, alarmed by the obstreperous barking of a great chained dog, ran out from some half-ruinous out-houses, and took charge of the horses; […]

glosses: To produce a warning of approaching danger or necessary action; to emit a signal intended to rouse a recipient to vigilance or put them on the alert.

examples.text: The tower cab supervisor and various pilots stated that the LLWAS system frequently alarms because of the thunderstorm activity present, and that airspeed losses are common as a result of convective wind shear.

glosses: To surprise with apprehension of danger; to fill with anxiety in regard to threatening evil; to excite with sudden fear.

examples.text: The loud bang in the hallway seemed to alarm everyone in the building.

glosses: To keep in excitement; to disturb.
A minor fright.

examples.text: Johnny had a bad scare last night.
England were held to a draw after surviving a major scare against Switzerland as they were forced to come from two goals behind to earn a point in the Euro 2012 qualifier at Wembley.

glosses: A cause of terror or alarm; a panic; something that inspires fear or dread.

examples.text: a food-poisoning scare

glosses: A device or object used to frighten.

examples.text: But I admit the possibility of their being used as "scares" for either birds of prey or snakes, or both.

glosses: To frighten, terrify, startle, especially in a minor way.

examples.text: Did it scare you when I said "Boo!"?
That cannot be; the noise of thy crossbow / Will scare the herd, and so my shoot is lost.
Late triumphs of Russian science are scaring the very dogwater out of large elements in our society, and we both fear more "purging" instead of more effort at catching up.

(Laurel Stevenson) Would you please be quiet? You're scaring the little girl.
(Craig Toomey) Scaring the little girl?! Scaring the little girl?! Lady!

In other words, the transaction is preferred because it is the best of bad choices. And at least one study has found that when management preannounces a deal it results in lower premiums presumably because it scares off other bidders.

Residents of Sihu Township in the central county of Yunlin were left scared and angry after hundreds of dead geese were found dumped in an irrigation channel Tuesday, inciting a minor panic as avian flu continues to spread throughout the country.

glosses: (To be able) to be scared.

examples.text: I don't scare easily.

heftige Emotion, die durch die Wahrnehmung von etwas Unerwartetem oder Bedrohlichem ausgelöst wird

glosses: durch ein unerwartetes, schreckliches Ereignis ausgelöstes Entsetzen

examples.text: Der Schrecken sitzt mir immer noch in den Gliedern.
„Ob des erlittenen Schreckens nahm Frau Mondtraut Abstand davon, weiter hinaufzugehen.“

glosses: schreckliche Eigenschaft, schreckliche Seite von etwas

examples.text: Er hatte die Schrecken des Krieges hautnah erlebt.
„Für mich stand das in einem merkwürdigen Kontrast zu all den Schrecken, die auf den Bildern zu sehen waren.“

glosses: jemand, der Angst und Schrecken^([1]) verbreitet

examples.text: Er war der Schrecken der sieben Meere.

examples.text: Il fut saisi de frayeur.
Je ne suis pas encore bien revenu, bien remis de la frayeur que j’ai eue.
Il est dans des frayeurs continuelles.
Alors, pour lui éviter les frayeurs, n’actionnez pas le signal d'alarme à la légère.
